name: Clematis

project_scope.selection_mode: four canonical learner concepts; native-range tags kept separate
project_scope.note: All four present in canonical manifest. Sweet autumn clematis is an introduced, non-native look-alike learner only. Clematis reticulata is currently a research draft, not canonical and not assigned a native PASS.

shared_traits: woody or perennial climbing vines with opposite leaves
petal-like sepals rather than true petals
achenes often bearing persistent elongated styles/beaks
priority: length and plumosity of achene beaks
study_strategy.warning: Do not identify leatherflowers by color alone; sepal margin architecture and fruit beaks are critical.
study_strategy.look_here_first: Verify opposite leaves on a vine, then find ONE flower/fruit cluster. Open four-sepal flowers: compare native dioecious C. drummondii and introduced many-flowered C. terniflora. Nodding leathery urn-shaped flowers: compare C. pitcheri and C. texensis by the edge of a SEPAl, not just flower color. Later inspect an actual seedhead: plumose long beaks versus short appressed-haired beaks.
photo_teaching_order: opposite leaf node, leaflet attachment and climbing leaf stalk
open vs urn flower side views
hairy edge and rolled tip of four sepals in pitcheri / thick noncrispate margins in texensis
seedhead showing individual achene, persistent style and plumose hairs
paired leaves for drummondii versus terniflora

quick_key.if: Open pale flowers, often male/female flowers on different plants; leaflets divided/lobed; later a mass of VERY long silvery feathery achene tails
quick_key.then: Clematis drummondii — native old man's beard

quick_key.if: Open white/cream small flowers in large branched MANY-flowered sprays; opposite mostly 3–5 leaflets with smooth, ENTIRE edges
quick_key.then: Clematis terniflora — introduced sweet autumn clematis; native-only tally excluded

quick_key.if: Nodding leathery urn, four thick but distally THIN EXPANDED/CRISPATE sepal margins with recurved points; mature seed beaks ~1–3 cm little-appressed-hairy
Nodding leathery urn, unexpanded THICK noncrispate sepal margins and recurved points; mature seed beaks 4–7 cm PLUMOSE

curation_status.genus_audit: canonical learner four species, introduced terniflora correctly separate, retain target-zone labels
curation_status.photo_install_verification: 10 physical exact-species photos total (5+1+2+2), 0 new warnings

shared_genus_characters.look_here_first: Confirm a climbing vine with opposite leaves, then inspect the flower: the showy parts are sepals, not petals. Use mature sepal shape and the later achene head for species-level work.
shared_genus_characters.shared: Project Clematis are climbing perennials with opposite leaves, petaloid sepals, numerous stamens and pistils, and aggregate achenes with persistent styles.

species_comparison_matrix.reproductive_system: dioecious; male and female vines separate
species_comparison_matrix.photo_need: male flower front, female flower, leaf node and plumed ripe seedheads

species_comparison_matrix.flower: OPEN small white 4-sepal flowers in many-branched sprays
species_comparison_matrix.leaves: opposite compound, usually 3–5 unlobed ENTIRE-edged leaflets
species_comparison_matrix.reproductive_system: flowers generally bisexual; verify stamens+pistils on one flower
species_comparison_matrix.achene: flattened rimmed achenes with feathery styles
species_comparison_matrix.photo_need: one inflorescence with leaf and a macro of smooth edged leaflet

species_comparison_matrix.flower: nodding urn; four sepals with thin distal margin expansion to about 1 mm, often crinkled/recurved
species_comparison_matrix.photo_need: sepal edge side macro with arrow, achene side with ruler

species_comparison_matrix.flower: nodding scarlet urn; four sepals, thick unexpanded noncrispate margins
species_comparison_matrix.leaves: opposite leathery 1-pinnate leaflets, often glaucous below
species_comparison_matrix.photo_need: matched sepal edge side macro against pitcheri and fruit hair comparison

overlap_and_cautions: Flower color is secondary; inspect sepal margins and tips.
Opposite divided leaves establish the genus but do not reliably separate these species.
Use mature fruit for achene-beak comparisons.
If a mature sepal edge is not visible, keep a leatherflower ID provisional.

realistic_lookalikes.separate_by: Require Clematis reproductive architecture: petaloid sepals, many free stamens and pistils, then aggregate achenes with persistent styles.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.purpose: Show open flower versus urn and expose the sepal tips.
Show expanded/crispate/recurved versus non-expanded sepal margins.
Compare persistent style/beak length and plumosity.

diagnostic_review_handoffs: If mature sepal-tip structure cannot be verified, request a targeted flower-side macro rather than forcing the species ID.
Any species outside the current three-species project set goes to Taxonomy + Diagnostic Review before scope changes.

comparison_cards.title: Native old man's beard vs introduced sweet autumn clematis
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Not all white Clematis are the same: count flowers on a branch, then look at individual compound LEAFLETS (deeply divided/lobed in drummondii vs mostly entire and oval in terniflora). On drummondii separate male/female vines; on terniflora flowers mostly bisexual. Both can develop fluffy seed structures.
photo_requirements: leaf blade edge closeups at the same scale
individual male/female flowers versus bisexual bloom
mature seedhead with single fruit beak
comparison_cards.caution: Do not identify merely from fluffy silver seedheads; both produce plumed styles.

comparison_cards.title: Purple versus scarlet leatherflowers
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Find one sepAl EDGE near the tip: pitcheri = narrowly expanded thin CRISPATE margin, texensis = thick not expanded not crispate. Later verify fruit: pitcheri ~1–3 cm weakly hairy beak vs texensis 4–7 cm plumose beak.
photo_requirements: matched lateral urns at same scale
high resolution sepal edge macro arrows (true sepal margin not a petal)
two ripe achenes with cm ruler
comparison_cards.caution: Purple-versus-red hue is not a sufficient diagnosis in intermediate cultivated flowers; need wild species concept and sepal/fruit structure.

comparison_cards.title: Leatherflower or open-flowered clematis?
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Clematis has no true petals: the colored flower parts are four SEPALS. In the leatherflowers they join visually into a nodding urn; in drummondii and terniflora they spread openly.
photo_requirements: label sepals, stamens and central female parts

photo_priority: paired exact sepal margins pitcheri vs texensis
single female flower C drummondii, distinct from male
paired mature leatherflower achenes with rulers
